products.name: Sucralose
products.short: Zero-calorie sweetener, about 600 times sweeter than sugar.
products.tagline: Sucralose: Indulge in Sweetness Without the Calories.
products.html:
Sucralose is a zero-calorie artificial sweetener that is commonly used as a sugar substitute in a wide range of food and beverage products.

Here are some key points about Sucralose:

  • Sweetness and Taste: Sucralose is highly stable, making it suitable for use in a variety of food processing conditions. It remains stable at high temperatures, making it suitable for use in baking and cooking applications.
  • Caloric Value:Sucralose itself is calorie-free because it is not metabolized by the body. It passes through the digestive system without being broken down and does not contribute to the caloric content of food or beverages.
  • Flavor Profile: Sucralose provides a clean, sweet taste without any bitter or metallic aftertaste that is sometimes associated with other artificial sweeteners.

Applications

Sucralose is used in a wide range of food and beverage products, including:

  • Soft Drinks: It is used to sweeten diet sodas and other carbonated beverages without adding calories.
  • Baked Goods:Sucralose is used in the production of various baked goods, such as cakes, cookies, muffins, and bread, to reduce sugar content while maintaining sweetness.
  • Dairy Products: It is used in yogurts, ice creams, and other dairy products to provide sweetness without adding calories or affecting the texture.
  • Confectionery: Sucralose is used in candies, chewing gums, and other confectionery items as a sugar substitute.
  • Sauces and Dressings: It is used in sauces, dressings, and condiments to reduce sugar content while maintaining the desired sweetness.
  • Pharmaceuticals: Sucralose is sometimes used as a sweetener in pharmaceutical products, including syrups, chewable tablets, and liquid medications.

Safety

Sucralose has been extensively tested and approved for use as a food additive by regulatory authorities, including the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA). It is considered safe for consumption within acceptable daily intake limits.

products.name: Aspartame
products.short: Low-calorie sweetener for beverages, dairy and sugar-free food.
products.tagline: Aspartame: Delight in Sweetness with a Low-Calorie Advantage.
products.html:
Aspartame is an artificial sweetener that is widely used as a sugar substitute in a variety of food and beverage products.

Here are some key points about aspartame:

  • Sweetness and Taste:Aspartame is approximately 200 times sweeter than table sugar (sucrose), which allows for a significant reduction in the amount of added sugar in food and beverages. It provides a sweet taste without the caloric content of sugar.
  • Composition and Metabolism:Aspartame is made up of two amino acids, phenylalanine and aspartic acid, linked together with a methyl group. When consumed, aspartame is broken down into its individual components in the body and metabolized
  • Caloric Value:Aspartame is virtually calorie-free. Because it is not metabolized like sugar, it provides a sweet taste without contributing to the caloric content of food or beverages
  • Flavor Profile: Aspartame provides a clean, sweet taste without a noticeable aftertaste. It is often preferred over other artificial sweeteners due to its similarity to the taste of sugar.

Applications

Aspartame is used in a wide range of food and beverage products, including:

  • Carbonated Beverages: It is used to sweeten diet sodas and other carbonated drinks as a sugar substitute.
  • Tabletop Sweeteners:Aspartame is available in powdered or tablet form for individual use as a sugar substitute in coffee, tea, and other beverages
  • Baked Goods: It is used in the production of various baked goods, such as cookies, cakes, and pastries, to reduce sugar content while maintaining sweetness.
  • Dairy Products: Aspartame is used in yogurts, flavored milk, and other dairy products to provide sweetness without adding calories.
  • Confectionery: It is used in sugar-free candies, chewing gums, and other confectionery items as a sugar substitute.
  • Pharmaceuticals: Aspartame is sometimes used as a sweetener in certain pharmaceutical products, including chewable tablets, syrups, and oral suspensions.

Safety

Aspartame has been extensively studied and approved for use as a food additive by regulatory authorities worldwide, including the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA). It is considered safe for consumption by the general population, except for individuals with a rare genetic disorder called phenylketonuria (PKU), as aspartame contains phenylalanine.

products.name: Xanthan Gum
products.short: Thickener and stabiliser for sauces, beverages and dairy.
products.tagline: Xanthan Gum: Embracing Texture and Stability for Superior Food and Industrial Applications.
products.html:
Xanthan gum is a polysaccharide that is commonly used as a food additive and thickening agent.

Here are some key points about xanthan gum:

  • Natural Origin:Xanthan gum is produced through the fermentation of carbohydrates by the bacterium Xanthomonas campestris. It is considered a natural ingredient and is widely accepted in various food and industrial applications.
  • Thickening and Stabilizing Properties:Xanthan gum has excellent thickening and stabilizing properties, making it a popular ingredient in food and beverage formulations. It forms a viscous gel or solution when dispersed in water, enhancing the texture, viscosity, and mouthfeel of products.
  • Versatile Applications:Xanthan gum is used in a wide range of food and beverage products, including

Applications

Xanthan gum is used in a wide range of food and beverage, pharma products, including:

  • Sauces and Dressings: It is commonly used in salad dressings, sauces, gravies, and condiments to provide thickness and improve the overall texture
  • Bakery Products: Xanthan gum helps improve the elasticity and structure of dough, resulting in better quality bread, cakes, and other baked goods. It can also extend the shelf life of baked products by retaining moisture
  • Beverages:Xanthan gum is used in beverages to stabilize suspensions, prevent sedimentation, and provide a smooth mouthfeel. It is often used in dairy alternatives, fruit juices, smoothies, and other liquid products
  • Dairy Products: : It is used in dairy products such as ice cream, yogurt, and cream to improve texture, prevent ice crystal formation, and enhance stability
  • Gluten-Free Products: Xanthan gum is a common ingredient in gluten-free recipes as it helps mimic the texture and binding properties of gluten in baked goods.
  • Compatibility: Xanthan gum is compatible with a wide range of ingredients and works well in both acidic and alkaline formulations. It can be used in conjunction with other thickeners and stabilizers to achieve desired texture and functionality.
  • Solubility and Heat Stability: Xanthan gum is soluble in both cold and hot water, and it retains its functionality even at high temperatures, making it suitable for a variety of food processing applications.

Safety

Xanthan gum has been approved as a food additive by regulatory authorities worldwide, including the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA). It is considered safe for consumption by the general population, although some individuals may experience digestive symptoms in large amounts.

Overall, xanthan gum is a versatile and widely used ingredient that provides improved texture, stability, and mouthfeel to a variety of food and beverage products. Its ability to enhance viscosity and create desired product characteristics makes it valuable in the food industry.

products.name: Citric Acid
products.short: Acidulant, flavouring and preservative for food and beverages.
products.tagline: Citric acid : Enhancing Flavor and Preservation in Food and Beverages.
products.html:
Citric acid is a natural organic acid that is widely used as a food additive, flavoring agent, and preservative.

Here are some key points about citric acid :

  • Natural Origin:Citric acid occurs naturally in citrus fruits such as lemons, limes, oranges, and grapefruits. It is extracted commercially from citrus fruits or produced through fermentation of sugars by certain microorganisms.
  • Acidic Properties:Citric acid is a weak organic acid with a sour taste. It is highly soluble in water and forms a clear, acidic solution.

Applications

Citric acid is used in a wide range of food and beverage products, including:

  • Flavor Enhancer: It is commonly used in salad dressings, sauces, gravies, and condiments to provide thickness and improve the overall texture
  • Acidulant: Citric acid is used as an acidulant to regulate the acidity (pH) of foods, especially in the production of canned goods, jams, jellies, and preserves. It helps inhibit the growth of bacteria and acts as a natural preservative
  • Antioxidant:Citric acid also functions as an antioxidant, which helps prevent or slow down the oxidation of food components, thus extending the shelf life of certain products
  • pH Adjuster: It is used to adjust the pH level of food and beverage formulations, providing balance and enhancing flavors
  • Cleaning and Household Products: Citric acid is a common ingredient in cleaning products, detergents, and household cleaners due to its ability to remove mineral deposits, rust stains, and soap scum. It is considered a safer alternative to harsher chemicals for certain cleaning applications
  • Cosmetics and Personal Care: Citric acid is used in a variety of cosmetic and personal care products, including skincare formulations, shampoos, conditioners, and bath products. It helps balance pH levels, acts as a preservative, and aids in exfoliation
  • Chelating Agent: Citric acid can function as a chelating agent, meaning it forms complexes with metal ions. This property is utilized in food preservation, as it can bind to metal ions that may promote spoilage or discoloration

Safety

Citric acid is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by regulatory authorities such as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA). It is considered safe for consumption in appropriate amounts. However, individuals with certain health conditions, such as citric acid intolerance or kidney problems, may need to limit their intake.

Overall, citric acid plays a crucial role in the food industry as a flavor enhancer, acidulant, and preservative. Its versatile properties extend beyond the food industry, finding applications in cleaning products and personal care items.

products.name: Monosodium Glutamate (MSG)
products.short: Flavour enhancer for savoury food.
products.tagline: Monosodium Glutamate (MSG): Elevating Flavors to New Heights.
products.html:
Monosodium glutamate (MSG) is a flavor enhancer commonly used in the food industry to enhance the taste of various dishes.

Here are some key points about Monosodium glutamate (MSG):

  • Flavor Enhancer:Monosodium glutamate is known for its ability to enhance the savory or umami taste in foods. It does not have a specific taste of its own but enhances the natural flavors of the ingredients in a dish, making them more pronounced and enjoyable.
  • Glutamic Acid:Monosodium glutamate is the sodium salt of glutamic acid, an amino acid naturally found in many foods, including meat, fish, vegetables, and dairy products. Glutamic acid is responsible for the umami taste, which is often described as a savory, meaty, or brothy flavor.

Applications

MSG is widely used in various cuisines and food products, including

  • Savory Foods: It is commonly added to soups, stews, broths, sauces, marinades, and gravies to enhance their flavor profiles and make them more appetizing
  • Processed Foods: MSG is used in many processed and packaged foods, such as snacks, frozen meals, canned soups, and ready-to-eat meals, to improve taste and palatability
  • Seasonings and Condiments:MSG can be found in seasoning blends, bouillon cubes, salad dressings, and sauces to enhance their taste and depth of flavor
  • Culinary Use: MSG can be used in home cooking to enhance the flavor of homemade dishes. It is often added in small amounts during the cooking process or sprinkled lightly on finished dishes as a seasoning
  • Compatibility: MSG is compatible with a wide range of ingredients and can be easily incorporated into various recipes. It dissolves readily in liquids and disperses evenly throughout the food

Safety

  • Safety and Regulation: Monosodium glutamate has been extensively studied and is generally recognized as safe for consumption by regulatory authorities, including the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA). It is considered safe for most people when consumed in normal amounts
  • Sensitivity and Allergies: Some individuals may be sensitive to MSG and may experience symptoms such as headaches, flushing, sweating, or a sensation of numbness or tingling. However, these reactions are rare, and MSG is not considered an allergen
  • Labeling and Usage: In many countries, including the United States, the use of MSG as an ingredient is required to be disclosed on food labels. This allows individuals who are sensitive or wish to avoid MSG to identify products that contain it

It's important to note that while monosodium glutamate is generally considered safe, individual sensitivities and preferences may vary. As with any food ingredient, moderation and balance are key when using MSG in cooking or consuming foods that contain it.

products.name: Potassium Sorbate
products.short: Preservative that inhibits mould and yeast.
products.tagline: Potassium Sorbate: Safeguarding Freshness with Natural Food Preservation.
products.html:
Potassium sorbate is a chemical compound that is commonly used as a food preservative to inhibit the growth of fungi, yeasts, and molds.

Here are some key points about potassium sorbate:

  • Preservation:Potassium sorbate is effective in preventing the growth of microorganisms, particularly yeast and mold. It works by inhibiting the reproduction and metabolism of these organisms, thereby extending the shelf life of food products.

Applications

Potassium sorbate is used in a wide range of food and beverage products, including:

  • Baked Goods: It helps prevent the growth of molds and extends the freshness of bread, cakes, pastries, and other baked goods
  • Dairy Products: Potassium sorbate is used in dairy items such as cheese, yogurt, and sour cream to inhibit the growth of yeasts and molds
  • Sauces and Dressings:It is commonly used in salad dressings, sauces, and condiments to prevent spoilage and maintain product quality
  • Beverages: Potassium sorbate is used in certain beverages, including fruit juices, wines, and carbonated drinks, to prevent fermentation and spoilage
  • Jams and Preserves: It is utilized in the production of jams, jellies, and fruit preserves to inhibit the growth of yeasts and molds and extend their shelf life

Chemical Properties

Potassium sorbate is a white crystalline powder that is highly soluble in water. It is a derivative of sorbic acid, which occurs naturally in certain fruits and berries.

Compatibility

Potassium sorbate is compatible with a wide range of food ingredients and processing conditions. It is stable under normal storage and processing conditions, but its effectiveness may be reduced at high pH levels or in the presence of certain organic acids.

Limitations

While potassium sorbate is effective against yeasts, molds, and fungi, it may not be as effective against certain bacteria or viruses. Therefore, it is often used in combination with other preservatives or processing methods to ensure microbial safety.

Applications

  • Water Retention:Potassium humate can improve the water-holding capacity of soils, reducing water stress on plants and helping them withstand drought conditions
  • Chelating Properties: It forms complexes with certain nutrients, such as iron, zinc, and manganese, making them more accessible to plants. This enhances nutrient uptake and improves overall plant health
  • Stimulates Plant Growth: Potassium humate has been shown to stimulate root growth, increase seed germination rates, and enhance plant vigor and productivity
  • Environmental Benefits: The use of potassium humate in agriculture can contribute to sustainable farming practices by reducing the need for synthetic fertilizers and minimizing environmental impacts, such as nutrient runoff and soil erosion
  • Compatibility: Potassium humate is compatible with various soil types and can be used in conjunction with other fertilizers and soil amendments. It is suitable for use in conventional farming, organic farming, and horticulture
  • Application Methods: Potassium humate can be applied to the soil through fertigation (via irrigation systems), as a soil amendment during land preparation, or as a foliar spray to provide direct nutrient uptake through plant leaves
  • Regulatory Considerations: The use of potassium humate in agriculture may be subject to specific regulations and guidelines in different countries or regions. It's important to consult local agricultural authorities or experts for proper usage recommendations and compliance

Overall, potassium humate is valued for its ability to improve soil fertility, nutrient availability, and plant growth. Its application in agriculture supports sustainable farming practices and contributes to healthier and more productive crops

products.html:

Here are some key points about SODA ASH:

  • Chemical Composition:Soda ash is primarily composed of sodium carbonate (Na2CO3). It occurs naturally in mineral deposits or can be synthetically produced through the Solvay process.
  • Production:Soda ash is produced on a large scale, both through natural sources like trona ore or sodium carbonate-rich brines, as well as through synthetic chemical processes that involve reacting sodium chloride with ammonia and carbon dioxide.
  • Industrial ApplicationsSoda ash finds extensive use in different industries, including

Applications

SODA ASH is used in a wide range of food and beverage products, including:

  • Glass Manufacturing: One of the major applications of soda ash is in glass production. It is used as a fluxing agent, helping to lower the melting point of silica, facilitating the formation of glass products

    • ⦁ Industrial Cleaning: It is used in cleaning agents, such as detergents, to sequester metal ions and prevent them from interfering with the cleaning process or causing undesirable reactions
    • ⦁ Agriculture:EDTA di-sodium is utilized as a chelating agent in agricultural applications, including soil remediation and hydroponics, to enhance nutrient availability and prevent metal toxicity
    • ⦁ Pharmaceutical and Medical: It is used in some medical and pharmaceutical applications, such as in chelation therapy to remove toxic metals from the body
  • ⦁ Analytical Chemistry: EDTA di-sodium is widely used in analytical chemistry for complexometric titrations and as a reagent for metal ion analysis. It is utilized to determine the concentration of metal ions in a sample by forming stable complexes that can be detected and quantified
